nodes.label: Courier-not-consumer mental model for PID data
nodes.rationale: The PID block is encrypted for UIDAI and signed by the device; neither the app nor Eko's servers can decrypt it. Your code forwards it untouched. Possession of decrypted biometrics would violate the Aadhaar Act, so never decrypt, parse, log or persist Skey/Hmac/Data — read only <Resp>.

nodes.label: UIDAI registered devices (L1 mandate)
nodes.rationale: UIDAI mandates L1 devices that sign and encrypt inside trusted hardware; L0 (host-software signing) is phased out and its captures can be rejected even when the local scan succeeds. Integration code is identical for both, so upgrading hardware does not change code.

nodes.label: RDService driver discovery on ports 11100-11120
nodes.rationale: Probe each port with the custom RDSERVICE verb over http then https; browsers allow HTTPS pages to call http://127.0.0.1 because loopback is exempt from mixed-content blocking. Find the CAPTURE interface by its id attribute, not by position, and sanitise the returned path (some drivers emit a full URL) rejecting any non-loopback host.

nodes.label: PidOptions XML configuration
nodes.rationale: Always send env="P" — Morpho rejects S/PP and Mantra fails when env is missing, and the UIDAI environment is chosen server-side anyway. Keep format="0" (XML) because many drivers return error 210 for Protobuf.

nodes.label: wadh digest binding capture to a KYC API version
nodes.rationale: base64(SHA-256(ver+ra+rc+lr+de+pfr)). Do not compute or guess it — use exactly the value the endpoint documents. Required for eKYC captures, omitted entirely for plain authentication captures. A missing or wrong wadh surfaces much later as 'Authentication Failed. Invalid Biometric data.'

nodes.label: qScore retry/block thresholds
nodes.rationale: Eko's production apps retry below 45 and block below 25 — a low-quality scan fails authentication at UIDAI anyway, so re-scanning early saves a round trip.

nodes.label: Android RDService integration via UIDAI Intents
nodes.rationale: Drivers are per-manufacturer Play Store apps responding to in.gov.uidai.rdservice.fp.INFO / .CAPTURE. Uses Eko's android-uidai-rdservice-manager library rather than hand-rolled Intent plumbing; the XML payloads are identical to the web flow. Mobile browsers cannot reach RDService because there is no localhost driver on a phone.

nodes.label: RdServiceTester in-browser device tester
nodes.rationale: Runs the documented flow entirely in the reader's browser so integrators can verify hardware first and diff their own request log against a known-good one.
